inputs.original_text: A former Israeli prime minister’s adviser, Daniel Rubenstein, says a political resolution is vital, yet the message still centers Israel’s “unwavering stance” against Iran’s nuclear and missile programs and describes the operation as ongoing. That tension matters: lasting security cannot come from military action alone. A political path must address the wider structures driving conflict and put the safety and rights of people across the region ahead of endless escalation.
inputs.modified_text: Daniel Rubenstein’s call for a political resolution is important, but it sits uneasily beside a message still organized around Israel’s “unwavering stance” and an ongoing operation. That is the problem with treating military pressure as the center of security: it can perpetuate the very conditions that keep people across the region unsafe. A durable resolution has to confront the structures behind the conflict and protect people’s rights, not make endless escalation sound like the only option.
